title: SOLID Principles
description: Master the five SOLID principles for better OOP design.

data.text: **SOLID** is an acronym for five design principles that make software designs more understandable, flexible, and maintainable.

items: S - Single Responsibility: A class should have one reason to change
O - Open/Closed: Open for extension, closed for modification
L - Liskov Substitution: Subtypes must be substitutable for base types
I - Interface Segregation: Many specific interfaces > one general interface
D - Dependency Inversion: Depend on abstractions, not concretions

data.title: Single Responsibility
Why SOLID Matters
data.text: SOLID principles reduce technical debt and make systems easier to test, extend, and refactor.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Each class should do one thing well
data.takeaway: SOLID principles are the foundation of maintainable OOP.
